en: The Philippine eagle is the national bird and requires large tracts of dipterocarp forests to hunt and nest.
The Ifugao people built the Banaue Rice Terraces using ancient stone-walling techniques that create a sustainable irrigation system.
The Supreme Court, the highest judicial branch of government, is headquartered in a neoclassical building in Manila.
The Pahiyas Festival in Lucban celebrates the rice harvest by decorating houses with colorful kiping made from rice paste.
The Sampaguita, the national flower, is a fragrant white jasmine that blooms year-round in the tropical Philippine climate.
A statue in Mactan, Cebu commemorates Lapu-Lapu, the indigenous leader who defeated Ferdinand Magellan in the 1521 battle.
The Bohol tarsier is one of the smallest primates and has specialized eyes that cannot rotate within their sockets.
Baybayin, an ancient pre-colonial writing system, uses vowel-consonant syllables and was traditionally carved into bamboo or palm leaves.
The 1987 Philippine Constitution guarantees the right to free public education for all citizens from elementary through high school.
Doctor Fe del Mundo designed a bamboo incubator for rural areas lacking electricity to keep premature babies warm.
Abaca, a native banana plant, produces strong fibers that are traditionally harvested and woven into ropes and textiles.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan features a navigable underground river that flows directly into the sea.
